### ISSUE-M1: Ambiguous Double-[14] Cross-Citation Notation

**Severity:** MODERATE
**File:** `agentic-research-best-practices.md`, line 277
**Check category:** 5 — CONTRADICTION / 9 — CROSS-REFERENCE LINKS

**Actual text:**
```
Trust-adaptive interventions [72] ... achieve −38% inappropriate reliance and +20% decision accuracy
— larger effects than the prior calibrated-confidence result (41.3%→28.2% from [14] via
`../agentic-research-bias/citations.md` [14]).
```

**Problem:** `[14]` appears twice — first as a bare citation number (local [14] = PRISM, USC, persona prompts), then as a cross-reference citation number in the bias repo. Local [14] has no connection to calibrated-confidence results; it covers expert persona accuracy penalties. The phrase "from [14] via `../agentic-research-bias/citations.md` [14]" is intended to say "from citation #14 in the bias repo," but the bare `[14]` before the cross-reference backtick causes a false local citation signal.

**Expected:** The notation should either (a) not use bare `[14]` and only reference the bias-repo citation by its repo-qualified form (e.g., "see `../agentic-research-bias/citations.md` [14]"), or (b) omit the bare `[14]` entirely since it does not correspond to a local PRISM citation. As written, a reader interpreting `[14]` as local will attribute the 41.3%→28.2% finding to PRISM (persona accuracy), which is wrong.

**Status:** OPEN

### ISSUE-N1: "~60% of Human Expert Baseline" Is an Unmarked Derived Estimate

**Severity:** MINOR
**File:** `retraction-log.md`, line 18
**Check category:** 7 — ESTIMATION MARKERS

**Actual text:**
```
the best agents reach ~60% of the human expert baseline, not ~4% of it.
```

**Derivation check:** o1-high reaches 24.4%; human ML PhD baseline 41.4%. 24.4 / 41.4 ≈ 58.9%, rounds to ~59%, close to ~60%. Sonnet BasicAgent: 21 / 41.4 ≈ 50.7%. The "~60%" figure uses o1-high (the best agent) not Sonnet BasicAgent (the corrected subject). This is internally consistent and the tilde marker is present, but the derivation (24.4 / 41.4) is not stated. The prior "~4%" comparator uses 1.8 / 41.4 ≈ 4.3%, which also checks out. The estimates are sound but the arithmetic derivation is implicit.

**Status:** OPEN (low-risk; no material error, but derivation transparency could be improved)

**Severity:** MINOR
**File:** `citations.md`, lines 186, 191, 219, 224, 229, 234, 240, 276, 281, 308, 328, 338, 343, 348, 353, 380, and [87]

**Severity:** MINOR
**File:** All 6 reference files (`references/*.md`)
**Check category:** 8 — CAVEAT HONESTY

This matters because `references/source-verification.md`, `references/prompt-engineering-agents.md`, and `references/human-in-the-loop.md` each contain turn-level or interaction-level quantitative findings (e.g., self-consistency rates from [22], agent self-pause rates from [16], clarification trigger percentages) that are specifically flagged by [87] as subject to autocorrelation inflation.
